result.title: A Benchmark Protocol and Fairness Analysis Towards Open-Set EEG Seizure Type Classification
result.comment: Accepted at the IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV) 2027 Workshop. Code and evaluation protocol are publicly available
result.summary: Automated EEG seizure type classification systems are typically trained and evaluated under the closed-set assumption, where all seizure types encountered at deployment are seen during training. In clinical practice, this assumption fails: patients present with rare or atypical seizure types that fall outside the training label space, and a system that forces a wrong label is worse than one that abstains. We introduce the first open-set recognition protocol for EEG seizure type classification on the Temple University Hospital Seizure Corpus (TUSZ v2.0.3), defining known and unknown classes using the clinical taxonomy itself: seizure types with sufficient subject representation (at least 12 subjects) form the known set, and rare types form the unknown set. We evaluate seven post-hoc open-set scorers (MSP, MaxLogit, energy, Mahalanobis, kNN, GHOST, and COSTARR) applied to a partially fine-tuned EEG Foundation Model (EFM), using a subject-disjoint leave-one-class-out (LOCO) protocol over three seeds that tests whether methods can detect seizure types excluded from fine-tuning. On true unknown classes, the best scorer (Mahalanobis) reaches a mean AUROC of 0.66, and differences among the top scorers are within seed-to-seed variation. Held-out known seizure types from unseen subjects are detected only slightly above chance (AUROC 0.54-0.58 for all scorers). Per-subject rejection rates are highly uneven for all scorers, and GHOST does not significantly improve per-subject fairness over energy scoring (two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank, p >= 0.25). We release the protocol, subject splits, and code as an initial baseline; our results indicate that open-set seizure type recognition remains a hard, open problem.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文在 TUSZ 癫痫语料上提出首个 EEG 发作类型开集识别协议，用临床分类学把常见类型划为 known、罕见类型划为 unknown，并在部分微调的 EEG 基础模型上评测七种 post-hoc 开集打分器与被试级拒绝公平性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「宁可弃答也不强行给出错误标签」的选择性预测设定，以及按被试统计的拒绝率不均，可能为 LVR 中 STOP 决策与证据不足时的弃答评价提供参照，但属远端临床领域、未涉及视觉 latent 状态，仅供核查。
